sections.text: Higher education in the United States is an extraordinarily fragmented, decentralized, market-based system producing enormous inequality in quality and outcomes. It is simultaneously the envy of the world (top research universities), deeply dysfunctional for large segments of the population (student debt, credential inflation, low completion rates), and under fundamental political and economic stress.

```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  HIGHER EDUCATION LANDSCAPE                      |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  INSTITUTIONAL TYPES             FINANCING                       |
|  -----------------               ---------                       |
|  Community colleges (2-yr)       Tuition (net price)             |
|  State universities (4-yr)       Pell Grants (federal)           |
|  Research universities (R1)      Student loans (federal)         |
|  Private liberal arts            Institutional aid               |
|  For-profit                      Endowment income                |
|  Flagship + land-grant           Research grants                 |
|                                  State appropriations            |
|                                  (declining % of budget)         |
|  GOVERNANCE                                                      |
|  ----------                      CRISES                          |
|  Boards of trustees              Student debt ($1.7T)            |
|  President/administration        Credential inflation            |
|  Faculty (tenure system)         Adjunct labor crisis            |
|  Accreditation bodies            Affordability crisis            |
|  State legislatures              For-profit predation            |
|  Federal government              Political/culture wars          |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
